project.name: Private Anime Streaming Platform
project.goal: Build a personal-use anime-style streaming platform with Jellyfin as the media backend and a custom React frontend.

timeline.summary: The project started as a single Vite React app with a stylized anime discovery UI inspired by consumer streaming sites.
The original dashboard-like prototype was redesigned into a more premium streaming-home layout with glassy panels, a cinematic hero, and content rails.
The app direction changed from a standalone front-end mockup to a production-oriented hybrid architecture using Jellyfin as the streaming backend and a custom UI as the primary product surface.
The repo was restructured into a monorepo with separate client, server, and docs folders.
A local Jellyfin instance was installed and its startup wizard was completed with safe localhost-first defaults.

configuration_status.current_blocker: The app still needs a real Jellyfin API key and user ID in server/.env before end-to-end library and playback tests can run against the live server.

sonarr.conclusion: Sonarr can be useful as a lawful organizer and automation tool for media the user already has rights to use, but Jellyfin remains the actual streaming backend.

next_recommended_steps: Log into Jellyfin and create an API key.
Find the Jellyfin user ID for the configured admin user.
Populate server/.env with JELLYFIN_URL, JELLYFIN_API_KEY, and JELLYFIN_USER_ID.
Run npm run dev:server and npm run dev:client.
Add real Jellyfin libraries and verify browsing, detail pages, and HLS playback.
Tune the UI against real poster and backdrop assets from the live library.
